title: Staged Variant Safety Net with Auto-Retract Policy and Metric Synthesis
creator: Anika Rao
description: Implement a staged-variant safety net that automatically retracts (rolls back) A/B or staged variant rollouts when a synthesized quality gate indicates regression. This ticket covers the evaluation orchestration, signal synthesis (unit and composite metrics), decision policy engine, and the rollback actuator integrated into the rollout controller. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect real regressions and remove manual intervention for common, quantifiable failures while keeping a clear human-in-the-loop path for ambiguous cases.
background: Current canary/A-B flows require manually defined single-metric thresholds in several places which leads to missed multi-dimensional regressions and noisy alerts.

We need richer, contextual gates that combine generation quality signals (perplexity proxies, rerank delta, hallucination heuristics), latency/cold-start regressions, and token-cost anomalies into a single decision signal.
This ticket builds on the staged rollout controller and evaluation collectors (see dependencies) and introduces a lightweight policy synthesizer and an auto-retract actuator.
Primary customer: platform and ML teams shipping model/config flips to hosted and dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: System can subscribe to a rollout and evaluate per-variant metrics over a sliding window (configurable: default 10k requests or 15 minutes).
Composite quality gate built by synthesizing weighted signals (quality, latency, cost) returns a boolean decision with an explainable provenance blob.
When the gate trips, controller triggers automatic retract to the immediate previous stable variant and records the action to the audit log and rollback history.
On retraction, system notifies oncall and the originating PR/owner via Slack/email with a summary and link to evidence dashboard.
False-positive rate measured in the staging experiment must be <= 5% across 4-week rolling test window when evaluated against known regressions/controls.
Runbook and monitoring dashboards created in Console (route-level chart + traffic cohort diffs) and linked in PR.
E2E test harness validates retract behavior for both canary (gradual percentage) and A/B (split traffic) rollouts under deterministic synthetic regressions.
tasks: Design policy synthesis format and developer UX for weighting signals (PM/Design review)
Extend collector to export new quality signals: n-gram hallucination heuristics, rerank-score-delta, answer-consistency checks
Implement decision engine microservice (stateless) with simple provenance output and confidence score
Add retract actuator to rollout controller with safe throttling and idempotency
Build dashboard and evidence links in Console; include traffic cohort diff visualization
Write e2e tests and chaos experiments that simulate latency spike, hallucination injection, and cost regression
Create runbook and oncall playbook for manual override and audit review
Security review for auto-retract actuator and audit logging
design_notes: Prefer composable linear scoring for the first iteration (score = sum(w_i * normalized_signal_i)) to keep provenance easy to explain.
Allow per-project/route overrides for weights; default safe profile used for platform-managed deployments.
Decision engine returns: verdict (pass/fail), score, top contributing signals (for explainability), and sample evidence links.
Rollback actuator will use the controller's existing rollback API but must add: reason code, triggered_by=auto_retract, evidence_url, and a cool-down window to avoid flip-flop.
We will keep a manual 'dry-run' mode during initial rollout where verdicts are emitted but not actioned; telemetry still collected.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Automatic retraction reduces MTTR but risks blocking risky, noisy signals from long-tailed traffic; mitigated via cool-down and min-sample thresholds.
Complex composite gates can be harder for teams to reason about than single-metric thresholds; include explainability and an 'open the hood' report link.
False positives during early rollout could erode trust—start with conservative weights and dry-run for two weeks before enabling auto-actuation.
Operational burden: more dashboards and alert types; will require a short-term increase in SRE oncall rotations during ramp-up.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize policy format, signal list, and wiring in collectors (ENG + Applied ML)
Week 2: implement decision engine prototype behind feature flag and wire dry-run verdicts to Console
Week 3: integrate retract actuator with rollout controller and add audit logging + notifications
Week 4: run canary on internal routes (10% traffic) with deliberate regression injections and refine weights
Week 5: enable auto-retract for select non-critical customer tenants and monitor; iterate on thresholds
Week 6: full rollout and handoff to platform + runbook completion
